comments.content: This JSON handling only applies when `$isSearchForcedCaseInsensitive` is true, but the `lower()` wrapping is applied unconditionally afterwards. On MySQL/MariaDB, `lower(json_extract(...))` works, but the previous behavior for JSON columns on MySQL/MariaDB (without this branch) would have been `lower(column->path)` which MySQL does not support as a function call — so this is a fix. However, note that `json_extract` returns a JSON value (e.g. quoted string `"foo"`), and `lower()` on that will include the surrounding quotes, which may not match the search term. Consider using `json_unquote(json_extract(...))` so the lowercased value matches the raw string. Also, this branch is skipped when `$isSearchForcedCaseInsensitive` is false, leaving `column->path` unhandled for the non-lowercased path — verify that's intentional.
